newsitem.title: THAILAND: Public outcry on Thai police killing of gunmen.
newsitem.headline: Public outcry on Thai police killing of gunmen.

text.p: Thai police faced an outcry of public criticism on Thursday, a day after after officers killed six alleged drug traffickers who had already surrendered to police.
Newspapers carried harsh editorials and outraged callers flooded radio and television stations to accuse the police of overreacting in the situation.
Police shot dead six gunmen in Suphan Buri, about 150 km (90 miles) northwest of Bangkok, on Wednesday after the men had surrendered and released three hostages they had held overnight.
Police said they were forced to shoot the suspected drug traffickers -- who were in handcuffs -- because they had tried to fight back.
Witnesses who saw the dead bodies said the men had all apparently died from gunshots to the back of their heads.

"The deaths of six men in police custody in Suphan Buri have shocked the nation," the Bangkok Post said in an editorial. "The story...indicate possible extrajudicial killing by police. This was the impression gained by witnesses."
Callers to radio stations were sceptical of the police claim that they had killed the suspects because the men had resisted.
"How can suspects who are handcuffed fight back against police?" one caller asked, echoing comments made by many others.
Others said the police did not have the right to take justice into their own hands, even if the suspects were known to be involved in illegal actions.

"There is no doubt that the (suspects) were criminals and apparently all had police records that testified to a vicious streak," the Bangkok Post said. "What must be answered is whether the police who took them into custody also were vicious."
"Officers on the job, and their superiors, know their duty does not extend to that of prosecutor and judge. Justice is a matter for the judicial system," it said.
